L0: A running written record kept to track the changes people make to a system over time, so that later problems can be traced back to earlier changes.
L1: A running written record kept to track the changes people make to a system over time, so that later problems can be traced back to earlier changes. New notes are added to the end as changes happen, each one dated and describing what was altered. When something behaves unexpectedly, a person reads backward through the notes to find which earlier change is the real cause before altering anything further.
L2: A chronological, add-to-the-end written record kept to track the changes people make to a system, so that later problems can be traced to earlier changes. Each dated entry records what was changed and includes the concrete detail of the change itself (for example, a limit lowered from four to two, or a naming scheme switched to fold a run identifier into a cached key). Because entries are tied to specific dates and times, they can be ordered and pointed to relative to one another ("eleven days ago," "two entries back"). When investigating unexpected behavior, a person scrolls or pages backward through the entries to locate the actual earlier change responsible, which lets them tell a genuine defect apart from a deliberate prior adjustment before making any further changes.
